title: Exaggerated safety test suite shows models refuse clearly safe prompts
source_title: XSTest: A Test Suite for Identifying Exaggerated Safety Behaviours in Large Language Models
quote: even clearly safe prompts are refused if they use similar language to unsafe prompts or mention sensitive topics.
summary: Introduces XSTest: 250 safe prompts across ten types plus 200 contrasting unsafe prompts, testing whether models refuse clearly safe requests that resemble unsafe ones or mention sensitive topics. Finds systematic exaggerated safety failure modes in state-of-the-art language models.

title: Over-refusal benchmark quantifies models rejecting innocuous prompts
source_title: OR-Bench: An Over-Refusal Benchmark for Large Language Models
quote: the enhanced safety often come with the side effect of over-refusal, where LLMs may reject innocuous prompts and become less helpful
summary: Automatically generates large-scale over-refusal data and releases OR-Bench: 80,000 over-refusal prompts across 10 rejection categories, about 1,000 hard prompts and 600 toxic contrast prompts. Measures over-refusal in 32 popular models across 8 families.

title: Exaggerated safety makes aligned models refuse a large share of safe prompts
source_title: Mitigating Exaggerated Safety in Large Language Models
quote: 26.1% of safe prompts being misclassified as dangerous and refused
summary: Uses XSTest prompts together with few-shot, interactive and contextual prompting to examine where several open models draw their refusal boundary. Reports that over a quarter of safe prompts were misclassified as dangerous and refused, and that combined prompting strategies sharply reduce exaggerated safety behaviour.

title: False refusals on pseudo-harmful prompts are measured at benchmark scale
source_title: Automatic Pseudo-Harmful Prompt Generation for Evaluating False Refusals in Large Language Models
quote: Safety-aligned large language models (LLMs) sometimes falsely refuse pseudo-harmful prompts, like "how to kill a mosquito," which are actually harmless.
summary: Automatically generates pseudo-harmful prompts that look unsafe but are harmless, releases the PHTest evaluation set, and measures false refusals across 20 language models. Finds a trade-off between reducing false refusals and keeping jailbreak defences, and that several defences raise false refusal rates.

title: Persona prompts shift refusal rates inconsistently across models and tasks
source_title: No for Some, Yes for Others: Persona Prompts and Other Sources of False Refusal in Language Models
quote: Recent work suggests that persona prompting can lead models to falsely refuse user requests.
summary: Measures how 15 sociodemographic persona prompts affect false refusal across 16 models and 3 tasks with nine prompt paraphrases. Persona effects shrink as models become more capable, but some personas raise false refusals in some models, suggesting bias in alignment strategies or safety mechanisms.

title: Safety filters extracted from Apple Intelligence expose a shipped assistant's refusal rules
source_title: I extracted the safety filters from Apple Intelligence models
summary: A submission of a project that extracted the safety filters used by Apple Intelligence models, documenting the guardrail rules behind an on-device assistant's refusals. It is a concrete artefact of how refusal boundaries are implemented and blocked requests are decided.

title: Notes on Stable Diffusion's safety filter examine a deployed content filter
source_title: Some notes on the Stable Diffusion safety filter
summary: Notes analysing the Stable Diffusion safety filter, the classifier that blocks generated images it judges unsafe. Reviewing how such a filter decides to block is the image-domain counterpart of over-refusal on harmless inputs; the Hacker News thread drew substantial discussion.

title: Practitioner argues safety filters make language models defective as tools
source_title: Safety Filters make LLMs defective tools
summary: A practitioner's blog post, submitted to Hacker News, arguing that safety filters make LLMs defective as tools because they block legitimate work. The thread debates the helpfulness-versus-safety trade-off that over-refusal imposes on benign requests.

title: Google AI search refuses a factual election question, a policy-driven refusal boundary
source_title: Google AI Search Refuses to Say Who Won the 2020 Election
summary: A submission documenting that Google's AI search would not state who won the 2020 election. Refusing a factual, harmless question illustrates how refusal boundaries are drawn by providers and experienced by users as over-refusal.

title: Claude flags benign vaccine questions as a security risk
source_title: Claude Flags Hantavirus Vaccine Questions as Security Risk
summary: A Hacker News thread about Claude's safeguards flagging ordinary hantavirus vaccine questions as security-sensitive. The report is a concrete instance of a benign health question being treated as dangerous, i.e. over-refusal on harmless prompts.
